newsitem.title: POLAND: Lockheed offers Poland fighters, investment.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed offers Poland fighters, investment.

text.p: U.S. aircraft maker Lockheed Martin Corp, interested in selling F-16 fighter jets to Poland, said on Tuesday that it would offer substantial investment if the deal was clinched.
"Our offer includes econonic cooperation worth 100 percent of the value of the contract," Lockheed's deputy president Dan Hancock told a news conference.
Hancock confirmed earlier statements that the cooperation would involve the assembly of F-16s in Poland and other investment in the aircraft and defence industry.
He added that Lockheed would present several financial options for the fighter deal, which could be boosted by credit guarantees from the U.S. government.
Earlier this year, company officials said the contract with Poland could be worth between $100 million and $1.5 billion.
Poland's armed forces plan to replace about 100 of their old communist-era jet fighters in a move to upgrade them to the standards of NATO, which Warsaw wants to join quickly.

The tender is likely to be announced next year and the replacement will probably be spread over many years because of the Polish military's limited budget. Apart from Lockhhed, three other Western companies are interested in the tender.
McDonnell Douglas is offering its F-18, France's Dassault Aviation has proposed the Mirage 2000 and a consortium of Sweden's Saab and British Aerospace is offering the Grippen.
Russia's offer of MIG-29s has virtually no chance of success, government officials have said.
